overall: No violation found: the Committee could keep 2020 collective-bargaining executive session minutes sealed at the time of the request because the bargaining was still ongoing, though the AG recommended periodic review and warned minutes cannot be withheld indefinitely.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee kept minutes of 2020 collective-bargaining executive sessions sealed after publication would no longer defeat their purpose.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it withheld executive session minutes because the purpose for keeping those minutes confidential still existed at the time of the request for minutes.

allegations.summary: Not framed as a separate allegation: notices cited Purpose 2 but discussions were Purpose 3 strategy; the letter checked whether the topic description was adequate.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the executive session topic listed on the relevant notices was sufficiently descriptive and described the actual discussions that the Committee engaged in during the executive session meetings, which was strategy for negotiations with the Sharon Teachers’ Association collective bargaining unit.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
